title: Peacock Celebrates 70 Years With The Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon
site_name: Fratello Watches - The Magazine Dedicated To Luxury Watches
excerpt: ✓ Peacock celebrates 70 years with the Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon ✓ Two impressive references ✓ Read more here! ✓
content:
Two variants with impressive levels of finishing and watchmaking

Peacock is celebrating its 70th anniversary with a pair of timepieces that treat the dial as an impressive curved stage. One of China’s longest-standing manufacturing houses, the brand places a free-sprung central tourbillon at the center of these watches. Concentric hour and minute markers orbit the movement, evoking the astronomical event that provides the models their name. Let’s have a closer look at the new Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon.

As we’ll see, the Peacock Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon focuses as much on the movement as on the métiers d’art surrounding it. A hand-executed curved guilloché pattern, coined “Gravitational Weave,” covers the dial surface. V-shaped grooves contract toward the center, creating the black-hole effect. Plus, each dial is unique because the artisan must continuously adjust pressure and angle by hand. This results in stunningly detailed watches that owners can truly call their own.

The Peacock Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon

The Peacock Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon is available in two options — the Cloud Azure and the black-coated Night Purple. Both use circular, lugless Grade 5 titanium cases measuring 43.5mm wide and 11.9mm thick, including the substantial domed sapphire crystal. One is black-coated, while the other has a natural finish, and satin brushing and polished highlights appear on each case. Each also has a 5atm water resistance rating.

An integrated strap runs from 23mm to 18mm wide and closes with a matching coated or natural Grade 5 titanium pin buckle. This results in a lightweight watch with a modern look.

An impressive guilloché dial

The Gravitational Weave guilloché pattern is the dominant characteristic on the Black Hole models.  To make this form, Peacock had to adapt its equipment to work with the arc-shaped bezel. In total, 240 interlocking V-grooves are present on the dial, with each requiring six separate manual passes. Yes, this feature requires an impressive 1,440 cuts, each opening at a 3° angle.

After the engraving, the surface is finished with abrasive media, yielding a matte finish. This ensures each cut catches light more effectively. Interestingly, Peacock heat-treats the guilloché ring, creating a light blue hue on the Cloud Azure and a purple finish on the appropriately named Night Purple.

Additional heat-treated features

Another distinctive element is the inner ring framing the tourbillon. Like the case, this is Grade 5 titanium. It is micro-hollowed with a laser and flame-blued by hand at incredibly high temperatures. This results in colors ranging from deep purple to electric blue, and like the guilloché ring, it looks slightly different on every watch. To display the time, concentric titanium discs carry the hours in blue Super-LumiNova BGW9 lume and the minutes in green C1 lume. These discs orbit the tourbillon’s cage and fit the space concept.

An in-house tourbillon

Peacock’s manual-winding caliber PAX9611A sits beneath the dial. First, the four-barrel movement allows 120 hours of power reserve and ticks at 21,600 vph (3 Hz). Then, like the detailed internal bezel, the movement’s rear plate also receives engraving. All of this is visible beneath a screw-in case back with sapphire crystal.

Thoughts and pricing

The Peacock Black Hole III Curved Guilloché Central Tourbillon models cost US$5,099. That’s impressive for an in-house, centrally mounted tourbillon with a five-day power reserve. Yes, this watch comes from a country other than Switzerland, but with a 70-year history, Peacock presents an interesting option for those who value haute horlogerie and value for money. For more information, visit the official Peacock website.
